public_rationale: The words 'They don't work at all' reply to the line 'Agents will automate large parts-', and the same passage cites 58% and 35% success rates. The contract reads the claim as: agents could not reliably and autonomously complete multi-step work or do an entire job. That reading is supported. The literal wording, that agents do not work at all, is not supported, because the sources show partial success. Salesforce AI Research's CRMArena-Pro preprint (May 24, 2025) found leading agents reached about 58% single-turn and about 35% multi-turn success on its business tasks, and over 83% single-turn success on Workflow Execution (e1). METR (March 2025) found frontier models such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet had a 50% time horizon of about 50 minutes on its software tasks (e3). That means success on bounded tasks about half the time, not dependable autonomous work. A CMU-led benchmark abstract dated September 10, 2025, after the post, reported that the best agent completed 30% of tasks autonomously (e2). It is used as context only. No item in the packet shows agents reliably doing whole jobs.
limitations: The outcome rests on the contract's contextual reading. The literal claim that agents do not work at all is not supported, because the same sources show partial success.
No standard reliability threshold defines when an agent 'works'.
The benchmarks may not reflect supervised, human-in-the-loop deployments.
The CMU-led benchmark figure comes from an abstract version dated after the post, so it is context only.
The METR figure covers software tasks only, and the CRMArena-Pro figures cover CRM business tasks only.

our_interpretation: Read in context, 'don't work at all' is not a claim that agents never succeed at any task. The speaker himself cites 58% and 35% success rates in the same passage. The plain reading is that AI agents do not work as boosters describe them: they cannot reliably and autonomously complete multi-step work or do an entire job.
Test: did the best available measurements before the post show agents failing to complete realistic multi-step professional tasks reliably and autonomously?
Target period: January 2025 to the post date (August 2025). This is the most recent state public evidence could report before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Independent or credible benchmark evidence from the period shows that leading agents fail a large share of realistic multi-step business or workplace tasks, well short of dependable autonomous job performance.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence from the period shows that agents reliably and autonomously complete realistic multi-step professional work at high success rates, or do whole jobs.

evidence.excerpt: Experiments reveal leading LLM agents achieve only around 58% single-turn success on CRMArena-Pro, with performance dropping significantly to approximately 35% in multi-turn settings.
evidence.explanation: Leading agents failed about two-thirds of realistic multi-turn business tasks. That supports the contextual claim that agents do not work as dependable autonomous workers.
